hero.title: Kling 4.0 — direct the scene, references and sound
hero.intro: Kling 4.0 brings scene direction, reference-guided generation and video editing into one model family. Plan the action, framing and sound together; use the mode that matches the material you already have.

faqs.a: Kling 4.0 is Kuaishou’s video model with documented text, image, reference and editing workflows. This page presents its provider contract and preparation guidance.

faqs.q: Can I generate with Kling 4.0 on MaxVideoAI now?
faqs.a: Yes. App, Studio and MCP offer Kling 4.0 for text, image, references and video editing, subject to compatible inputs and a current quote. The functional checks do not certify the artistic quality of a new render.

faqs.q: What durations and resolutions are documented?
faqs.a: The schema accepts whole-second durations from 3 to 30 seconds and 720p or 1080p output. Five seconds and 1080p are the generation defaults. Editing can inherit source duration when duration is omitted.

The provider announces native stereo audio, dialogue, singing and lip synchronization. The documented endpoints have no audio toggle or audio-file input. These are provider claims, not measured MaxVideoAI audio results.

faqs.q: Are first and last frames supported?
faqs.a: Image-to-video requires an opening image and accepts an optional ending image. Reference generation accepts an optional opening image but does not document an ending-image parameter. Neither mode exposes a timed keyframe array.

The generation modes accept a list of shot prompts. Each shot prompt is limited to 512 characters, and its duration is an integer from 1 to 30 seconds. Shot durations must sum to the requested 3–30-second clip. No explicit maximum shot count is published in the inspected schema.

faqs.q: What can I use as a reference?
faqs.a: Reference generation accepts up to 10 images, including an optional opening image, up to 5 video references and up to 7 elements. The provider announces a 15-asset overall budget. Reference videos and video elements share 30 seconds; each video must be 3–30 seconds. Element constraints must also be respected.

The reference-generation element schema includes a voice ID, with a maximum of three voice-bearing elements. Voice creation and operational use remain separate qualification steps. Ordinary text and image generation do not expose a voice list.

Editing requires a source video and a prompt and accepts optional reference images and image elements. It does not expose multi-shot, voice elements or an aspect-ratio control. Its input and output duration both affect provider billing.

faqs.q: Will older Kling examples be replaced?
faqs.a: Existing Kling model pages and videos keep their original identities, prompts and settings. A Kling 3 or Omni video does not become a Kling 4.0 example.

section.title: Prompt Lab — Kling 4.0
section.intro: These are original draft prompts to adapt, not prompts from completed Kling 4.0 renders.
section.tip: Make the subject, action, camera and sound unambiguous. Timed shots guide the sequence; they do not guarantee exact cuts.

tabs.label: Scene direction
tabs.title: Ignition — unrendered film prompt
tabs.description: A customer sabotages his repaired motorcycle to stay near the mechanic. She sees through his excuse and offers him a helmet. Original proposal; no Kling 4.0 render has been generated or evaluated.
tabs.copy: An adult romantic film scene in a small motorcycle repair shop at closing time. A sharp-faced woman in her fifties, with tied brown hair and one broad white streak, wears open blue coveralls over a dark vest. Her customer is a man in his sixties with an aquiline nose, carefully combed gray hair and a camel coat too elegant for the workshop. She reconnects one accessible cable on his old motorcycle, wipes her hands and turns toward the bench. He checks that she is looking away, then quietly disconnects the very same cable. In the reflection of the shop window, she sees what he has done. Let her look at him for a moment before he notices. She returns, reconnects the cable and holds his gaze. Without scolding him, she takes two plain helmets from the shelf, offers one to him and keeps the other. She says softly in English, "You could just ask." His practiced composure gives way to an embarrassed, relieved smile. She smiles back. End with the two helmets between them and the invitation understood. Warm late-afternoon light, tangible grease and worn leather, restrained performances. Follow the cable only long enough to explain his excuse; give the discovery and final exchange more room. Sound: workshop ambience, the connector, cloth, helmets and her natural voice. A few quiet notes of original guitar may enter after his smile. No additional dialogue or text.

tabs.label: Opening image
tabs.title: A careful reveal
tabs.description: Adapt this prompt to your own opening image.
tabs.copy: Continue from the supplied image. Preserve the subject, materials and lighting. Move the camera slowly to the right while the subject makes one small natural movement. End on a steady composition. Soft room ambience.

tabs.label: References
tabs.title: The same character, a new scene
tabs.description: Use only references you have permission to use.
tabs.copy: Use the supplied references to preserve the adult character’s face, clothing and proportions. Place the character in a quiet railway station at sunrise. They look toward an arriving train, then take one deliberate step forward. A gentle camera push, distant train sound, no dialogue.

tabs.label: Video editing
tabs.title: Change the atmosphere
tabs.description: Describe the intended change to your source video.
tabs.copy: Keep the people, movement and composition of the source video. Change the setting to a warm late-afternoon atmosphere with softer shadows and subtle golden light. Preserve readable faces and natural textures.
